title: Remove stray spaces with TRIM
summary: Clean extra spaces from region names with TRIM so that comparisons and lookups find their match.

blocks.text: The regional sales targets are kept in a clean list: Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu and so on. The weekly sales files, however, come from several people, and some region names carry a stray space at the end, or two spaces in the middle.
You cannot see a trailing space, but Excel treats it as a real character, so "Nairobi " is not the same as "Nairobi" and a lookup fails. TRIM is the tool that removes these invisible spaces.

items: Objective: remove stray spaces with TRIM before matching text.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: TRIM removes all spaces from the start and end of the text, and replaces each run of spaces between words with a single space.
Clean the name first, then look it up. The quotation marks in the table above only show where the text starts and ends; they are not part of the text.

items: A space is a character: =("Nairobi "="Nairobi") is FALSE, and an exact-match XLOOKUP will not find it.
Use LEN to find invisible spaces: if a name looks like 7 letters but LEN says 8, there is a stray space.
TRIM changes only ordinary spaces. Spaces that come from some web pages and systems (non-breaking spaces) can survive TRIM.
Tip: do the cleaning in a helper column and match on the clean column, so the original data is never overwritten.

blocks.text: Type numbers without commas or spaces, for example 12.

items: TRIM(text) removes leading and trailing spaces and reduces inner runs of spaces to one.
A stray space makes two names different: "Nairobi " does not equal "Nairobi".
LEN reveals hidden spaces: compare LEN(A2) with LEN(TRIM(A2)).
Look up the clean column, not the raw one.

blocks.text: Most "the lookup does not work" problems are invisible spaces, so TRIM first and match second.

items.prompt: What does =LEN(TRIM("  Kisumu   town ")) return? (The text has two spaces at the start, three between the words and one at the end.)
Cell A2 holds the text Nairobi followed by one space. What does =(A2="Nairobi") return?
What does =TRIM("Port   Reitz") return, if there are three spaces between Port and Reitz?

options.label: Port Reitz (one space between the words)

items.prompt: What does =LEN("  Eldoret  ")-LEN(TRIM("  Eldoret  ")) return? (The text has two spaces before and two spaces after the word.)
